fact_check.claim: Minimum stipend $4,076 a month before tax for 2026-27 ($48,912 over 12 months, $36,684 over nine)
fact_check.note: Page lists $36,684 (9-month) and $48,912 (12-month TA/GA/RA/GRA), effective Aug 21, 2026. No monthly rate is published; $4,076 is the correct division of both figures (36,684/9 and 48,912/12). University Fellowship 12-month is $44,463, not mentioned in the article.

fact_check.claim: Cost of attendance 2026-27: housing $19,962, food $5,768, books $2,464, transportation $3,754, personal $4,196; health insurance not included
fact_check.note: All figures match; page says the student health plan is excluded from cost of attendance.

fact_check.claim: Aid cannot cover rent in months you are not a registered student
fact_check.note: Page says aid can't help with 'covering rent during months that you are not a registered student'.

fact_check.claim: Aid does not cover security deposits or first and last month's rent
fact_check.note: Page lists 'security deposit, first/last month's rent' as not covered.

fact_check.claim: Cost of attendance can be raised case by case with documentation
fact_check.note: Page: 'determined on a case-by-case basis after a student submits appropriate documentation'; a budget-increase form is also required (not mentioned in article).

fact_check.claim: Downtown, Fall Creek and the Commons: lower rents, frequent bus service, 20 to 30 minute uphill walk
fact_check.note: Page says graduate students prefer these areas for 'lower rents', a 20 to 30-minute uphill walk, frequent service.

fact_check.claim: Downtown/Fall Creek/Commons have 'a city feel graduate students often prefer'
fact_check.note: Page says grad students prefer them for lower rents; a 'city feel' is not in the fetched text.

fact_check.claim: Collegetown is 0.1 to 0.5 miles from campus, but popularity raises rent
fact_check.note: Rent point is correct, but the page gives a walk of up to 15 minutes (lower Collegetown is uphill), not a 0.1 to 0.5 mile distance.

fact_check.claim: Lansing and the Northeast are less expensive and somewhat remote, so you need a bus or a car
fact_check.note: Page: generally less expensive, lengthy level walk, recommends bus or car, lines run regularly. 'Somewhat remote' is a paraphrase; acceptable.

fact_check.claim: West Hill rents lower, winter heating very high, ask NYSEG for average yearly bills
fact_check.note: Page says rents less costly, heating bills can be very high, check NYSEG at (800) 572-1111 for yearly averages.

fact_check.claim: Hasbrouck studio $1,355; one-bedroom $1,415 to $1,490; single in two-bedroom townhouse $620 to $910; 12-month contracts
fact_check.note: Page: studio $1,355, 1BR unfurnished $1,415 / furnished $1,490, townhouse singles $620 (regular) and $910 (large), 12-month contract.

fact_check.claim: Housing rates include gas, electricity, garbage pickup and internet up to 200 GB a month
fact_check.note: Page states this for housing rates generally, not as a Hasbrouck-specific note; the article's 'Confirm eligibility' hedge covers it.

fact_check.claim: Student health plan $4,092 for 12 months; $2,046 per semester for returning fully funded students; new fall 2026 students pay $1,705 fall and $2,046 spring
fact_check.note: All figures match.

fact_check.claim: Registered PhD students and graduate assistants receive free TCAT OmniRide passes
fact_check.note: Quoted nearly verbatim by the page.

fact_check.claim: Other degree-seeking students ride free after 6 p.m. on weekdays and all day on weekends
fact_check.note: Page adds conditions the article omits: registered, enrolled in a degree program, and in school for a year or more. Weekend wording on the page is 'all day on Saturdays and Sundays'.

fact_check.claim: NY DPS estimates $241 a month for natural gas heating Nov-Mar 2026-27 at 140 therms, and about $74 a month electric supply at 600 kWh; varies by region; electric is supply only
fact_check.note: Figures match. 'Supply only' wording is consistent with the page's 'supply'.

fact_check.claim: 209 Stewart Ave: room at $850 a month all-in with heat, water, electricity, WiFi; lease Aug 1, 2026 to Jul 31, 2027; deposit one month's rent; five-bedroom in Collegetown
fact_check.note: All match. The listing also adds a $20 county solid waste fee and $80 garbage fee split among five tenants at signing (about $20 each per year), so 'all-in' is slightly understated; the listing is on Ithaca College's housing site.

fact_check.claim: 1006 N Aurora St: $775 to $875 per room plus utilities, about a 19-minute walk to the Oval
fact_check.note: Rent and 'plus utilities' match. The page shows 'Your Commute: 19-minute' without stating a walk, and the description says less than 1/2 mile to campus; 'walk' is an assumption.

fact_check.claim: 709 N Tioga St: two one-bedrooms at $1,600 and $1,700; landlord pays internet and water; tenant pays electric and garbage tags
fact_check.note: Match. The page shows top-level price '$Ask' / 'Call For Price', and the $1,700 unit was available June 1, 2026; no availability date for the $1,600 unit, so 'advertised for the 2026-27 lease year' is not fully supported.

fact_check.claim: Maplewood: unique to graduate, faculty and professional students; electricity, trash, internet and cable included; $130 amenity fee per leaseholder at move-in; no rents published
fact_check.note: All match; the fee is a one-time charge due at move-in.

fact_check.claim: 2018 Grad Cafe thread: Assotto said downtown and Fall Creek are where most grad students live, studios started around $1,100, roommates about $600; Manuscriptess called Collegetown mostly undergrads
fact_check.note: Posts dated Jan 31, 2018. Manuscriptess said 'mostly upperclassmen undergrads and can be expensive'. Used only as dated student opinion, not a hard fact; rents are labelled as eight years old.
Recomputed from the listed monthly figures; correct. Monthly lines are the annual aid figures divided by 12 and rounded.

beats_top.query: cornell grad student off-campus budget monthly rent Ithaca cheap neighborhoods
beats_top.why: The top results are raw listings and an old forum thread with no budget, no stipend comparison and no utilities; ours answers in the first paragraph with a sourced monthly total set against the 2026-27 stipend. Weak spots are the Fall Creek column (electric left out, so the margin is overstated) and thin neighborhood rent guidance.
changes: Add an estimated electric line (the DPS $74 supply figure) to the Fall Creek column so its total and left-over are not overstated, or state the adjusted left-over in the text.

Make the neighborhood section tie to rents: give one price point per area (Collegetown, Fall Creek/Downtown, Lansing/Northeast) from the listings already cited, so 'cheap neighborhoods' in the query is answered with numbers.
Put the nine-month caveat in the opening paragraph or table, since a 9-month stipend of $4,076 only covers nine months of income against 12 months of rent.

fixes: Change 'Collegetown is 0.1 to 0.5 miles from campus' to say the neighborhood guide puts Collegetown up to a 15-minute walk from campus (lower Collegetown is uphill); source https://scl.cornell.edu/residential-life/housing/campus-housing/housing-search-process/ithaca-neighborhoods

Replace 'a city feel graduate students often prefer' with what the page says: graduate students prefer Downtown, Fall Creek and the Commons for lower rents; source https://scl.cornell.edu/residential-life/housing/campus-housing/housing-search-process/ithaca-neighborhoods

Change 'about a 19-minute walk to the Oval' for 1006 N Aurora St to 'a listed 19-minute commute to the Oval (the listing says less than half a mile to campus)'; source https://offcampus.housing.cornell.edu/city/ithaca-college-ny/listing/1006-n-aurora-st-ithaca-ny-14850-usa-237075

Add the conditions to the TCAT sentence: other degree-seeking students must be registered, enrolled in a degree program, and in school for a year or more to ride free after 6 p.m. weekdays and all day Saturday and Sunday; source https://fcs.cornell.edu/departments/transportation-delivery-services/sustainable-transportation-options/bus-services-privileges-passes

Change 'These listings were advertised for the 2026-27 lease year' so it does not cover the 709 N Tioga listing: say the $1,700 unit was listed as available June 1, 2026 and the $1,600 unit shows no availability date; source https://offcampus.housing.cornell.edu/city/ithaca-college-ny/listing/cosy-quiet-comfortable-fall-creek-gem.-238258

In the Stewart Avenue bullet, add that the listing also charges a $20 county solid waste fee and an $80 garbage fee split among five tenants at signing, so '$850 all-in' is accurate for rent only; source https://offcampushousing.ithaca.edu/city/ithaca-college-ny/listing/209-stewart-avenue-235095

Add about $74 a month for electric (NY DPS typical supply at 600 kWh; source https://dps.ny.gov/winter) as a line in the Fall Creek column, giving a total near $3,364 and about $712 left, and say the figure is supply only and varies; update the figure block, the 'If you are...' section and the FAQ range ($786) to match.

In the neighborhood section, add one rent price point per area taken from the cited listings (Collegetown $850 room, Fall Creek $1,600 one-bedroom, Hasbrouck $1,355 studio), and say Lansing/Northeast and West Hill have no listing in this article so no price is given; do not add unsourced numbers.

Add one sentence to the opening paragraph saying the $4,076 is the same monthly figure for a 12-month or nine-month appointment but a nine-month appointment pays for only nine months, so summer rent has to be planned separately.
